learning_outcomes.text: Understand the global meaning of Computer Science.
Understand how information is represented in the computer.
Identify and know the different structural components of a computer and their functionality.
Describe and analyze the structure and functions of an operating system.
Develop the capacity for abstraction and discipline as a basis for the analysis of information processing problems and their decomposition into parts using modular design techniques.
Apply algorithm design techniques to find the solution to a problem (structured programming).
Apply the acquired concepts in the design and elaboration of algorithms using high-level programming language syntax.
Manage information contained in databases and files.

assessment_rules: The course is evaluated in its ordinary call through continuous assessment or a final exam. During the course, continuous assessment tests are carried out (15% questionnaires, 15% programming practices, 70% programming exam). To pass continuous assessment, a minimum of 5 points must be obtained in each questionnaire, in the average of programming practices, and in the programming exam. Students who pass the continuous assessment components may choose to complete the continuous assessment or take the ordinary final exam, which accounts for 100% of the final grade and requires a minimum of 5 points. The extraordinary call is evaluated through a final exam, accounting for 100% of the final grade and requiring a minimum of 5 points.
